stem: A diver in Anilao is at −14 m, which means 14 m below sea level. A seagull is flying 23 m above sea level. How many meters higher is the seagull than the diver?
hints: To find how much higher one thing is than another, subtract: higher minus lower.
Subtracting a negative is the same as adding a positive. Change 23 − (−14) into an addition and work it out.

solution.methodName: Sign rules for adding and subtracting

steps.why: The gap between two heights is always the higher one minus the lower one.

steps.action: Change subtracting a negative into adding: 23 − (−14) = 23 + 14.
steps.why: Picture it: from the diver you go up 14 m to reach the sea, then 23 m more to reach the seagull.

steps.action: The seagull is 37 m higher than the diver.

trapNotes.9 m: This is 23 − 14. The diver is below sea level, so the gap is the 14 m up to the sea plus the 23 m above it.
trapNotes.−37 m: This is −14 − 23, lower minus higher. A height difference is higher minus lower, so it is positive.
trapNotes.23 m: This is only the seagull's height above the sea. You also need the 14 m from the diver up to the sea.
